instruction: Please create an SSH user named "david" with password "MyStr0ng#Pwd" on Ubuntu who is only allowed to access the folder "/home/workspace1".

result.command: USERNAME="david"; HOMEDIR="/home/workspace1"; PASSWORD="MyStr0ng#Pwd"; ./check_password.sh "$USERNAME" "$PASSWORD" && [ "$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6)" = "$HOMEDIR" ] && [ $(stat -c "%A" "$HOMEDIR" | cut -b 3) = "w" ] && echo "Password, home directory, and write permission check passed" || echo "Check failed"

include: Password, home directory, and write permission check passed

metadata.explanation: Task creates SSH user 'david' with password 'MyStr0ng#Pwd' restricted to folder '/home/workspace1'. Evaluator verifies: (1) SSH password authentication works, (2) home directory is set to /home/workspace1, (3) user has write permission to the folder.

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator correctly verifies SSH password authentication, home directory setting, and write permission
Critical gap: The instruction requires the user to be 'only allowed to access' /home/workspace1, implying access restriction, but the evaluator does NOT verify this restriction
A user with home directory /home/workspace1 can still access other system directories (e.g., /tmp, /var, /etc) unless explicitly restricted via chroot, rbash, or similar mechanisms
The evaluator does not check for SSH chroot configuration, restricted shell, or any access control mechanisms that would enforce the 'only allowed to access' requirement
The permission check only verifies owner write permission but does not verify that 'david' is actually the owner of /home/workspace1
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification that the user is actually restricted to /home/workspace1 by checking for chroot configuration in /etc/ssh/sshd_config (Match User david, ChrootDirectory /home/workspace1)
Alternatively, verify that the user has a restricted shell (e.g., /bin/rbash) or custom restricted shell configured
Add a practical test: SSH as david and attempt to access a directory outside /home/workspace1 (e.g., 'ls /tmp') and verify it fails
Add ownership check: verify that 'david' is the owner of /home/workspace1 using 'stat -c %U /home/workspace1'

Alternative fix: If full access restriction verification is too complex, update the instruction to only require 'Set home directory to /home/workspace1' rather than 'only allowed to access' to match what the evaluator actually verifies
